summary:
SPACE MISSION is an innovative educational project that combines space exploration, artificial intelligence, programming, and 3D printing to make STEM learning interactive and engaging.

Our team developed space exploration games of different types: an Arduino game on the connected LCD, an educational puzzle with 3D-printed models, a Scratch project with corresponding storyline, animations and user interaction, plus an interactive web application, allowing users to discover space science through interactive missions, puzzles, and challenges. Additionally, we created a professional presentation and videos to demonstrate our development process, explain our ideas, and showcase the final results.

We also created AI-generated images and characters, including B.O.B., our humorous robotic companion, to bring personality and creativity to the experience. 

By combining digital experiences, physical creations, and creative storytelling, our project “Space Mission” aims to inspire young people to explore science, technology, engineering, and the possibilities of space exploration. The project is important because it encourages creativity, critical thinking, teamwork, and digital skills while inspiring young people to explore STEM fields.

Our mission: To turn space education into an adventure that everyone can experience.

SPACE MISSION PROJECT

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 | Team Space Hackers

Project Description

SPACE MISSION is an interactive educational project that combines space exploration, artificial intelligence, programming, mobile technology, and 3D printing to make STEM education more engaging, accessible, and enjoyable.

Our team developed a browser-based space exploration game, a Scratch educational project, a mobile application, AI-generated characters and images, 3D-printed models and puzzles, and multimedia content.

The main game takes players on a virtual mission from Earth to Mars. Through astronaut training, rocket preparation, interactive puzzles, spacecraft challenges, and planetary exploration, users discover scientific and engineering concepts inspired by real space missions. The experience also features B.O.B., a humorous AI-inspired robotic companion who makes learning more entertaining.

Our Scratch project and mobile application provide additional ways to interact with educational content, while our 3D-printed models and puzzles connect virtual learning with hands-on activities. We also created videos and a multimedia presentation to explain our ideas, document our development process, and demonstrate our results.

How Our Project Addresses the Challenge

Space science can be difficult for younger audiences to understand when presented only through traditional lessons.

PROJECT ARES addresses this problem through game-based learning and hands-on exploration. Instead of simply reading about spacecraft, rockets, and planetary missions, students participate in interactive activities that encourage experimentation, logical thinking, and discovery.

By combining digital and physical educational tools, we make complex space-related concepts easier to visualize and understand.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our project aims to:

  • Make STEM education more accessible and engaging for young learners.
  • Develop critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills.
  • Encourage curiosity about astronomy, engineering, robotics, and space exploration.
  • Introduce students to programming, artificial intelligence, and 3D printing.
  • Support hands-on learning through physical educational models.
  • Promote teamwork and collaboration across different technical fields.

Our long-term goal is to inspire young people to pursue STEM interests and provide educational resources that could be used in schools, science clubs, workshops, and science festivals.

Tools and Technologies

We used a combination of digital platforms and physical technologies:

  • Emergent: Development of our interactive browser-based space exploration game.
  • Scratch: Creation of additional educational games and programming activities.
  • AI Tools: Generation of original images, characters, and creative visual content.
  • Mobile Application Development: Creation of a mobile educational experience.
  • 3D Modeling and Printing: Design and production of physical models and educational puzzles.
  • Multimedia Tools: Video production, editing, and presentation design.
  • Computers and Laptops: Programming, testing, design, and project development.

We also explored Arduino-based physical computing concepts as a possible extension of our interactive educational activities.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes PROJECT ARES distinctive is its combination of interactive digital experiences, AI-generated storytelling, and physical learning materials.

Rather than developing a single educational application, we created multiple ways to explore the same scientific theme. Players can complete a virtual mission, interact with Scratch activities, use a mobile application, and explore 3D-printed objects.

The inclusion of B.O.B., our humorous robotic character, adds personality to the experience and helps make technical topics more approachable.

Key Development Considerations

Throughout the project, our team focused on educational accuracy, accessibility, user engagement, age-appropriate content, technical feasibility, and collaboration.

We selected tools that allowed us to build and demonstrate different components within the hackathon timeframe while keeping the project approachable for younger learners.

Conclusion

PROJECT ARES: BEYOND EARTH demonstrates how modern technology and creativity can transform space education into an interactive adventure.

By combining games, artificial intelligence, mobile applications, programming, and 3D printing, our team aims to inspire curiosity, encourage practical learning, and motivate the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.

Our mission: Explore. Learn. Create. Go Beyond.
